key_insight: The local tangent residual (LTR) estimates whether turbulent-flow data could benefit from nonlinear compression before training an autoencoder.
engineering_relevance: LTR can help practitioners avoid costly autoencoder architecture searches and hyperparameter tuning when POD is sufficient.
method: Compute LTR from local data geometry without model training or a threshold parameter.
Use LTR to estimate the potential benefit of nonlinear dimension reduction.
Quantify trained-decoder nonlinearity using decoder linearisation error (DLE), comparing the decoder with a linearised surrogate.
evidence_signal: Across two vortex street cases and a turbulent wind-turbine wake, LTR reproduced dominant trends in autoencoder compression performance, with large nonlinear potential corroborated by large DLE.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to the investigated flows; LTR indicates compression potential rather than guaranteeing performance for a particular autoencoder.
paper_title: A Priori Estimation of the Non-Linear Compression Potential and Quantification of Autoencoder Non-Linearity in Turbulent Flows
